Write {"file_path":"D:\code\tutors\.claude\worktrees\agent-a749202cb1d754187\scripts\generate-release-notes.sh","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# generate-release-notes.sh
#
# Generate release notes from git log between two refs.
# Groups commits by conventional-commit type and lists merged PRs.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/generate-release-notes.sh <FROM_REF> [TO_REF]
#
# Examples:
#   ./scripts/generate-release-notes.sh v14.0.0 v15.0.0
#   ./scripts/generate-release-notes.sh v15.0.0          # defaults TO_REF to HEAD
#

set -euo pipefail

FROM_REF="${1:?Usage: $0 <FROM_REF> [TO_REF]}"
TO_REF="${2:-HEAD}"

echo "# Release Notes: ${FROM_REF}..${TO_REF}"
echo ""
echo "Generated on $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"
echo ""

# Collect all non-merge commit subjects
commits=$(git log --no-merges --pretty=format:"%s" "${FROM_REF}..${TO_REF}")

print_section() {
  local title="$1"
  local pattern="$2"
  local matches

  matches=$(echo "$commits" | grep -iE "^${pattern}" | sed -E "s/^${pattern}[:(]?\s*//" | sort -u || true)

  if [ -n "$matches" ]; then
    echo "## ${title}"
    echo ""
    while IFS= read -r line; do
      echo "- ${line}"
    done <<< "$matches"
    echo ""
  fi
}

print_section "Features" "feat"
print_section "Bug Fixes" "fix"
print_section "Refactoring" "refactor"
print_section "Documentation" "docs"
print_section "Chores" "chore"
print_section "Tests" "test"

# List merged PRs
prs=$(git log --merges --pretty=format:"%s" "${FROM_REF}..${TO_REF}" | grep -i "Merge pull request" || true)

if [ -n "$prs" ]; then
  echo "## Merged Pull Requests"
  echo ""
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    echo "- ${line}"
  done <<< "$prs"
  echo ""
fi

# Catch-all: commits that don't match any conventional-commit prefix
other=$(echo "$commits" | grep -ivE "^(feat|fix|refactor|docs|chore|test)" | head -50 || true)

if [ -n "$other" ]; then
  echo "## Other Changes"
  echo ""
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [ -n "$line" ]; then
      echo "- ${line}"
    fi
  done <<< "$other"
  echo ""
fi
"}

## Context

The current CHANGELOG.md's most recent entry is v11.3.0 (2024-01-09). The package.json is at v15.2.0. Four major versions are undocumented. The changelog file is very long (1002 lines) — you need to ADD new entries at the TOP, keeping all existing content.

## Key commits by era

## What to write

Add entries at the TOP of the file, before the existing `#### [2024-01-09]: Tutors 11.3.0` entry. Use the same format as existing entries. Group changes under version headers. Keep entries concise — summarize related commits into single bullet points. Use the format:

```
## [Unreleased]
- (empty, for future changes)

## v15.2.0 (2026-07)
### Features
- ...
### Fixes  
- ...
### Infrastructure
- ...

## v14.0.0 (2025-07)
...
```

Use a cleaner format with ## for versions and ### for categories (Features, Fixes, Infrastructure/Chores). This modernizes the changelog format going forward while keeping old entries as-is.

Also add a note at the very top of the file explaining the format:
```
# Tutors Changelog

> Changelog format updated from v12.0.0 onward. For automated release notes generation,
> see `guides/Release-Strategy.md`.
```

## Release Notes Tooling

Also create a new file `scripts/generate-release-notes.sh` — a simple shell script that generates release notes from git log between two tags/refs. It should:
1. Accept two arguments: FROM_REF and TO_REF (default HEAD)
2. Extract conventional-commit-style messages grouped by type (feat/fix/chore/refactor/docs)
3. Also list all PRs merged (grep for "Merge pull request")
4. Output markdown suitable for a GitHub release

Make it executable. Keep it simple — no dependencies, just git + bash.

"Update changelog through v15.2.0 and add release notes generator

four major versions of changes. Add release notes generation script
for future releases."
